title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page 84 of a typed English translation of a Russian paper; the margin note 'p. 213' refers to the original pagination. The phrase 'fibre space of straight lines' is a literal rendering of 'расслоение прямых', i.e. line bundle, which confirms the translation. The page has been interleaved with Grothendieck's handwritten 1965 notes on CM tori and the Galois action on Pic(A), which are the previous and next pages and are unrelated. The typed text is a step in an algebraic proof of an ampleness or projectivity criterion, of the kind proved by Nakai, Moishezon and Matsusaka.

(1) First argument: injectivity of h. There is a birational morphism h: V^{*(2^q m)} -> V'^{(2^q m)} between images of V under the maps defined by sections of multiples of the line bundle [E']. One supposes the local rings O_{Q'} and O_Q differ, where hQ' = Q. One takes a rational function x on V together with constants C_beta. Then Q lies in every zero divisor (x - C_beta)_0 on V', so Q lies in the image under h of each (x - C_beta)_0 on V*, intersected with an open set U*. Since x is regular on U*, these zero sets are pairwise disjoint there. Hence Q has infinitely many preimages, which contradicts finiteness. So O_{Q'} = O_Q, h is injective, and the corresponding map between the 2^q m and 2^q o_m embeddings is one-to-one.

(2) Second argument: induction on dimension via a hypersurface section. One takes a hypersurface in the projective space attached to f_{2^q o_m} that contains W but not the image V^{(2^q o_m)}. The section of the image is the image of a divisor E'_nu, the zero locus of a section of a multiple [nu E'] of [2^q o_m E']. By the induction hypothesis on E'_nu: H^1(E'_nu, O(nE')|_{E'_nu}) = 0 for n >= n(E'_nu), and [m'E']|_{E'_nu} is very ample. The page breaks off just before the standard exact sequence 0 -> O(nE' - E'_nu) -> O(nE') -> O(nE')|_{E'_nu} -> 0, which is used to lift sections and vanishing from the divisor to V.

This is classical machinery: the Serre vanishing and Kodaira embedding style of induction, as in Nakai's criterion and Moishezon's work on projectivity. It serves an embedding or ampleness theorem.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible on this fragment. The argument is standard, though it is only a fragment and the exact-sequence step is cut off.
Typing inconsistencies: the subscript 'h_{q^q m, 2^q o_m}' is very likely 'h_{2^q m, 2^q o_m}'. A closing parenthesis is missing in 'h((x - C_beta)_{0V*} ∩ U*'.

ideas.what: Injectivity of a finite birational map between projective models, proved by showing the local rings coincide; otherwise disjoint level sets of a regular function give infinitely many preimages.
ideas.modern_name: Zariski's Main Theorem style argument / separation of points by multiples of a line bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Zariski; used in Nakai, Moishezon and Matsusaka
ideas.where_published: Zariski's Main Theorem is treated in EGA III and EGA IV (not this particular argument)

ideas.what: Inductive proof of vanishing of H^1 and very ampleness by restricting to a hypersurface section (a divisor in |nu E'|) and using the induction hypothesis on that divisor.
ideas.modern_name: Hyperplane-section induction for ampleness (Nakai–Moishezon criterion, Serre vanishing)
ideas.where_published: Ampleness and cohomological criteria: EGA II, EGA III; SGA 6 / Hartshorne, Ample subvarieties (not by Grothendieck)

transcription_corrections: '0_Q', '0_{Q'}', '0_V', '0_{E'_nu}' should read O_Q, O_{Q'}, O_V, O_{E'_nu} (local rings and structure sheaves), not zero.
'(x - C_beta)_{0V'}' means the divisor of zeros (x - C_beta)_0 on V'.
'h_{q^q m, 2^q o_m}' is probably 'h_{2^q m, 2^q o_m}'.
'p. 213' is a margin reference to the pagination of the original Russian source, not part of the text.
In 'a mapping of the variety E' into a projective space', the variety should carry the subscript, i.e. E'_nu.
